title: Simulated Bank Rule — Mandatory Tax Return for Unsecured Loan Review
section: Underwriting Policy Part 1.4 — Tax Return Documentation
description: Simulated demo rule requiring ITR / Form 16 submission for comprehensive tax evidence verification.
text: [SIMULATED DEMO RULE] Where an applicant's requested loan amount exceeds INR 3,00,000, submission of the latest Income Tax Return (ITR) or Form 16 is mandatory. If the tax return is missing, the application cannot receive automated approval and must be flagged for DOCUMENT_FOLLOWUP to request the missing tax document from the applicant.
applicability: All retail loan applications with loan amount > INR 3,00,000

title: Simulated Bank Rule — Salary Credit vs Payslip Discrepancy Escalation
section: Underwriting Policy Part 2.3 — Income Variance Threshold
description: Simulated demo rule establishing variance limits between payslip net income and bank statement credits.
text: [SIMULATED DEMO RULE] A variance greater than 10.0% between the net salary stated on the payslip and the average monthly salary credit observed in the bank statement constitutes a financial discrepancy. Moderate discrepancies require underwriting clarification (STANDARD_REVIEW with note), whereas variances exceeding 25% or multiple conflicting records require OFFICER_INVESTIGATION.

title: Simulated Bank Rule — Critical Identity Mismatch Zero-Tolerance Policy
section: Fraud Prevention & KYC Part 3.1 — Primary Identity Mismatch
description: Simulated demo rule requiring immediate officer escalation when loan application name does not match KYC identity.
text: [SIMULATED DEMO RULE] When the primary applicant name on the loan application form does not match the name extracted from the government KYC document (Aadhaar/PAN/Voter ID), the system must immediately trigger a Critical Identity Mismatch override. Automated processing is suspended, Review Priority is elevated to HIGH, Risk-Evidence Matrix is set to INVESTIGATE, and the application is routed for mandatory OFFICER_INVESTIGATION to prevent synthetic identity fraud.
applicability: All loan applications across all product categories

title: Simulated Bank Rule — Statistical Rejection Risk Escalation Threshold
section: Credit Analytics Part 4.2 — Machine Learning Risk Review Threshold
description: Simulated demo rule governing applications with high historical rejection risk signals.
text: [SIMULATED DEMO RULE] Applications where the historical machine learning rejection-risk probability exceeds 65.0% (HIGH ML Risk level) must not be processed under standard underwriting pathways. Even if documentation is structurally complete, the application must be assigned to an experienced credit officer for OFFICER_INVESTIGATION to evaluate debt burden, risk factors, and secondary financial stability.
applicability: All personal loan applicants with elevated statistical risk

title: Simulated Bank Rule — Missing Mandatory Supporting Document Follow-up
section: Application Processing Part 5.1 — Document Package Completeness
description: Simulated demo rule specifying officer follow-up actions when mandatory documents are absent.
text: [SIMULATED DEMO RULE] If an application has missing mandatory supporting documents (such as Bank Statement or Tax Return) but exhibits no fraudulent identity mismatch, the application shall be categorized under Risk-Evidence Matrix category REVIEW with recommended action DOCUMENT_FOLLOWUP. The loan officer shall request the missing documentation from the applicant before rendering an underwriting decision.
applicability: All applications with document completeness status INCOMPLETE

title: Simulated Bank Rule — Salary Credit Reconciliation & Cash Deposit Policy
section: Underwriting Policy Part 2.4 — Salary Reconciliation & Cash Deposits
description: Simulated demo rule requiring salary credit correspondence and reconciliation for unverified cash deposits.
text: [SIMULATED DEMO RULE] Net monthly salary declared by the applicant must correspond directly with regular salary credit entries in the applicant's primary operational bank account statements. Any discrepancy exceeding standard deduction tolerances or unverified cash deposits requires reconciliation by underwriting.
